text:
Maya Chen: handing off — ongoing routing-service error spike impacting hosted API customers in EU region. getting paged for increased 5xx rate (~4.2% over baseline) and some elevated tail latency. primary -> me (Maya) is ending shift, Liam you are primary for next 6h, Nadia you are secondary. Greg is the escalation SRE on call. ops-bot posted the alert thread earlier.

Liam O'Neill: taking primary. quick summary: is this causing customer-facing errors (client 5xx) or internal retries?

Maya Chen: client-facing 5xxs and truncated streams for some streaming requests. we saw simultaneous small spike in request size and a skewed routing to a handful of nodes. CS-Bot has a small list of affected tenants (3 customers with >1% error surge). I've messaged CS to prep.

Nadia Singh: noted. any config changes in the last hour?

Maya Chen: no deploys during window. infra autoscaling kicked earlier but not enough. I have a mitigation in progress: temporarily enable conservative routing to avoid overloaded pod pool and scale a dedicated pool. commands I ran:

```
# temporarily pin routing to healthy pools
curl -X POST https://infra-api.internal/routing/override -d '{"policy":"avoid-skewed-nodes"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxxx'
# scale dedicated pool
kubectl scale deployment routing-dedicated-eu --replicas=8 -n infra
```

Maya Chen: also enabled prefix KV cache for common prefixes to reduce token-steam work. impact so far: 5xx down from 4.2% -> 2.8% on the last minute check.

ops-bot: ALERT: routing-service.eu-west-1 5xx_rate > 3% for 3m. Incident ID: INC-2026-REDWOOD-RTG.

Greg SRE: noted. can you paste one sample error stack or recent logs? we need to check if it's timeout vs upstream exception.

Maya Chen: sample error from proxy logs:

```
ERROR routing-proxy: request handler failed: upstream write: broken pipe (errno 32) path=/v1/stream gen_id=ab12cd
WARN kv-cache: miss for key prefix: "prompt/1234" duration=2.1ms
```

Maya Chen: looks like upstream write failures and some slow KV misses. I've routed ~15% of traffic to fallback model variants in us-east which are cheaper but lower-latency to test degradation profile. no customer complaints yet except automated CS alerts.

CS-Bot: Notified affected customers: acme-corp, beta-analytics, devlite. CS rep assigned: @marcus.

Liam O'Neill: plan for my handoff: keep routing override in place unless 5xx < 1% for 5m sustained. continue scaling dedicated pool if needed. runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/routing-backend-failures (see section "temporary routing override" and "fallback model routing").

Nadia Singh: I'll validate the cache warmup and check whether prefix cache eviction policy caused misses. possible quick fix: preload top N prefixes. TODO: run preloader job with recent top-prefix list.

Maya Chen: started preload job with last-24h top prefixes. job id: preload-2026-03-14-17. monitor at https://infra-internal/jobs/preload-2026-03-14-17.

Greg SRE: also check kernel network metrics on the skewed nodes — the broken pipe suggests connection resets. can someone run `ss -tanp | grep routing-proxy` on the two nodes flagged in the dashboard?

Liam O'Neill: I'll SSH into node eu-rg-12 and eu-rg-14 and check. if NIC flapping, we fallback to replacement node via `kubectl cordon`/`drain`.

Maya Chen: current mitigation status bullets:
- routing override enabled -> reducing skewed allocations (in progress)
- scaled routing-dedicated-eu -> 6 -> 8 replicas (done)
- prefix preloader job started (in progress)
- fallback model routing enabled for 15% (in progress)
- CS notified (done)

Greg SRE: good. escalation criteria: if 5xx > 3% for 10m or customer error reports > 2 customers escalate to ENG infra pager and product ops.

Nadia Singh: coverage gaps: my morning shift starts in 5h; if this persists into Asia region business hours, we need to coordinate with APAC oncall. Liam, add note in the incident doc for APAC followup.

Liam O'Neill: will do. I will also add a small synthetic test to hit streaming endpoints every 10s to measure tail.

Maya Chen: handover checklist for Liam:
- monitor `routing-service.eu-west-1` 5xx_rate and `stream_latency_p95` dashboards
- confirm prefix preloader completes and reduces KV misses
- keep CS updated (message template in runbook)
- if 5xx creeps > 4% revert fallback routing and open full rollback to last stable kernel build
- escalate to Greg if network errors persist after cordon/drain

Liam O'Neill: ack, taking over. I'll update thread every 15 mins and on any change. :telephone_receiver:

Maya Chen: thanks — closing my shift. ping me if anything blocks hard escalation, I'll be reachable via DM for 30m. :handshake:

ops-bot: SHIFT-HANDOFF logged: previous_primary=Maya Chen new_primary=Liam O'Neill secondary=Nadia Singh incident=INC-2026-REDWOOD-RTG

Liam O'Neill: (15m) 5xx now steady at 2.6%. prefix preloader progress 40%. starting node checks now.

Nadia Singh: (20m) saw a few reclaimed file descriptors on eu-rg-14 — increasing `net.core.somaxconn` temporarily as a test. will report results.

Greg SRE: (30m) watching NIC metrics, no hardware error counters yet. good signal. continue current mitigations.

Liam O'Neill: (60m) update: 5xx down to 0.9% sustained. prefix preloader finished, KV miss rate dropped 70%. routing override will be removed in 10m if stable. I'll leave a note for APAC handover if needed.

Maya Chen: thanks team.
